brief.headline: Tech Selloff Weighs on Markets; Schaeffler Block Deal & ICICI Bank Draw Focus
brief.summary: Global markets face heavy headwinds as tech shares tumble on AI return concerns and sticky US inflation. Domestically, traders eye large corporate block deals, strong banking momentum, and fresh US tariff proposals.

takeaways.text: Schaeffler AG is reportedly planning a 6% stake sale in Schaeffler India via a ₹3,188 crore block deal at ₹3,400 per share.
TVS Motor plans to invest ₹2,000 crore in Tamil Nadu over four years, creating 1,000 jobs through a non-binding memorandum.
ICICI Bank hits record highs with overwhelming analyst support, while NSE shares jump 5% to ₹2,324 following ICICI Securities' initiation.
The US proposes additional tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, which may reduce to 17% following a trade deal.
Wall Street stumbles as Nvidia shares drop and the Nasdaq 100 briefly enters bear-market territory amid intensifying AI sector scrutiny.
PhonePe revives its initial public offering plans, targeting a valuation between USD 12-15 billion for an early 2024 or 2027 window.
Siemens Energy India reports an 82% surge in Q4 FY26 net profit to ₹653 crore and recommends a ₹12 dividend.

sections.india: Domestic equities face early session cues from large corporate developments including Schaeffler India's ₹3,188 crore block deal and Tata Steel's ₹5,825 crore stake purchase in APL Apollo Tubes. Banking counters remain in focus with ICICI Bank touching record highs and Deutsche Bank partnering with Punjab National Bank. Meanwhile, TVS Motor announced a ₹2,000 crore investment in Tamil Nadu, and Siemens Energy India posted an 82% jump in Q4 net profit.
sections.world: Global sentiment turned cautious as US PCE inflation rose to 3.8% in October, keeping the Federal Reserve on track for further tightening. The US Trade Representative proposed additional tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, creating external headwinds. Meanwhile, the Bank of England left the door open for a December rate hike, and gold drifted to a more than one-year low.
sections.tech: Technology shares suffered steep losses globally, with the Nasdaq 100 briefly entering bear-market territory amid a severe AI-sector selloff. Nvidia faced heavy pressure and credit risk warnings following executive changes and Washington scrutiny over China chip access. Domestically, PhonePe revived its IPO plans targeting a $12-15 billion valuation, while Airtel announced a ₹1,200 crore investment for three data centres in Assam.
